Description Title: Repeated Behavior Score Drops Over an Extended Period Despite Positive Match History Hello Dota 2 Team, I am reporting a recurring issue with my Behavior Score and Communication Score that has been frustrating me for a long time. This is not an isolated incident. For an extended period, I have repeatedly experienced the same pattern: my scores increase after playing matches, but when the next 15-match summary is updated, they drop again. This cycle has happened multiple times, making it extremely difficult for me to maintain a score above the 3000 threshold required to access ranked matchmaking. After my latest 15 matches, my Behavior Score dropped from 3058 to 2953, a decrease of 105 points. My latest match summary shows: - 13 positive matches out of 15 - 29 Commends received - 0 abandoned matches - 0 Communication Reports - Excessive Reports: No - 2 reported matches I consistently try to play fairly and positively, often receive MVP awards, and receive numerous Commends. Despite this, my scores repeatedly fluctuate, and I keep losing access to ranked matchmaking. I understand that Commends and positive matches do not guarantee an increase in Behavior Score. However, the repeated nature of these drops over an extended period makes me concerned that there may be an issue with the scoring system or how my account's scores are being calculated. Could you please investigate this recurring issue or clarify what could be causing these repeated decreases? I can provide screenshots of my previous scores, updated scores, and match summaries as evidence. Thank you for your time and consideration. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots Description Hello Valve Development Team, I would like to report a possible issue with Dota 2's reporting and Behavior Score system. My Behavior Score recently dropped from 5,926 to 5,461, a loss of 465 points, and I received a temporary matchmaking restriction of approximately four hours. My latest Conduct Summary Matches evaluated: 15 Positive matches: 12 Reported matches: 3 Reports: 9 Reporting parties: 9 Communication reports: 0 Abandoned matches: 0 Commends: 21 Excessive Reports: Yes Description of the problem My account currently has communication restrictions due to its Behavior Score, meaning I cannot use text or voice chat. When teammates become toxic, I mute them, report inappropriate behavior when necessary, and continue playing normally. I use map pings to communicate gameplay information. Sometimes teammates repeatedly demand that I join fights that I believe are strategically unfavorable. When I choose not to participate in those fights to avoid unnecessary deaths, I suspect some teammates retaliate by reporting me. I understand that refusing a teammate's call does not automatically prove that their report is abusive. However, I am concerned that the reporting system may be penalizing legitimate strategic disagreements. Expected behavior Reports should be evaluated based on actual disruptive gameplay rather than simply disagreement between teammates. Actual behavior My account received nine reports across three reported matches, followed by a significant Behavior Score reduction and an approximately four-hour matchmaking restriction. I cannot confirm that these reports directly caused the restriction, but the timing raises concerns. Request Could the development team investigate whether the reporting system is correctly handling potentially retaliatory reports? If a system error is identified, I respectfully request that the resulting Behavior Score reduction and matchmaking restriction be reviewed and corrected where possible. Description Good afternoon. I feel like the politeness system in Dota undermines the team aspect of the game, because in a game where you need to coordinate and work together to find ways to win, people can’t speak in voice chat or even type a message in the chat. Before, if you didn’t like someone, you could just mute them in-game and keep playing, but now even good players have to play without a microphone and often lose games because of it. Solving this problem would also address the issue of multi-accounting, since people most often create new accounts because of communication score. Also, sometimes when you write in-game chat messages, people who want to restore their communication score will report you for no reason, and this can lower your communication score. Doesn't this seem absurd? How is it possible to receive a communication report or penalty in a match where my text communication is already completely restricted? The Dota 2 behavior score system appears to have a systemic issue in low-behavior brackets: reports seem to carry disproportionate weight compared to commends. For players whose communication is already muted, this creates a loop where playing well and winning leads to enemy reports, which keeps the behavior score low and prevents recovery. Environment Game: Dota 2 Platform: Steam, PC Account ID: unsoftiz Steam ID: unsoftiz Behavior score: ~1500 (now) , ~2500 (before) Duration: ~1-2 years Communication status: muted by system Winrate over period: 50-60%+ Matches played trying to recover: about 500-800+ Steps to reproduce Have a low behavior score (~1500) and muted communication. Play ranked matches and perform well (win lane, carry, high winrate). Win games or lose close games. Observe reports from enemy team (when winning) and teammates (when losing). Check behavior score after multiple games with commends. Expected behavior Commends should offset reports enough to allow recovery. Reports should be validated or weighted based on context. Muted players should not be punished for chat they cannot use. Playing well and winning should not trigger a net negative behavior score. Actual behavior Behavior score remains low or decreases. Reports appear to have near-100% success rate in low-behavior brackets. Commends do not seem to offset even a single report. Creates an endless loop: low score → reports weighted heavily → low score. Impact Dedicated players who want to play competitively are locked out of ranked matchmaking for years. The system was designed to punish toxic behavior, but it appears to punish performance and winning in low-behavior pools. Additional context I have spent thousands of hours and around $150 on this account. I want to grind to Immortal, but the behavior algorithm has blocked ranked matchmaking. I can provide match IDs, behavior score history, and screenshots for review. Request Please have the Dota team investigate how automated reports are weighted in low-behavior brackets, especially for players with muted communication and high winrates. If this is not the correct GitHub repo, please point me to the official issue tracker. If you need more information (match IDs, screenshots, etc.), let me know. Thanks. Description Hello. I have been playing Dota 2 for a long time, and I am writing not to dispute a ban or complain about a specific match. I want to draw attention to a problem in the Communication Score and report system that, in my view, harms the game and punishes innocent players. I agree that Behavior Score is a working and necessary thing. It genuinely restrains those who ruin games: AFK players, feeders, people who intentionally spoil the match. But Communication Score works differently, and here is the fundamental problem. Dota 2 is a team game where communication is critical. When a player is forcibly deprived of the ability to write and speak, it is not only he who suffers, but also his four teammates. You cannot call missing, you cannot warn about a gank, you cannot call for Roshan, you cannot coordinate a push. So the punishment of one person turns into a punishment for the entire team. At the same time, the game already has a mute button. Any player can mute any teammate or opponent and no longer see or hear them. It turns out that the forced silence system duplicates a function that every player already has, but does it for everyone at once, without their consent. A separate problem is the mechanism of reports for communication itself. It does not analyze what exactly a person wrote or said. A report triggers based on the number of complaints. Because of this, a "communication report" easily turns into a tool of revenge: a person can be reported for bad play, for an incomprehensible move, for disagreeing with someone's decision- and he will receive a silence, even though he insulted no one. This has been discussed in the community for a long time, including by well-known players and streamers. Dendi publicly said that the report system "just doesn't work"; Stray228 compared forced mute in a team game to a situation where a footballer is left on the field but forbidden to pass. So on paper, the idea of separating "behavior" and "communication" looks logical. The problem is in the execution: the system triggers too easily on false complaints and gives a normal player almost no opportunity to prove that he did nothing wrong. What, in my opinion, should be changed: 1)Remove the forced global mute, or at least make it "off by default," so that teammates can decide for themselves whether to hear this player or not. 2)Make it so that a communication report triggers only with real analysis of text or voice, and not based on the number of complaints. 3)Leave players under silence with basic pings and the chat wheel- they are not toxicity and are needed for the game. 4)Return reports to their original meaning: to punish for ruining the game, not for an "unpleasant manner of communication." I understand that this is not a technical support issue, but I ask you to forward this to the Dota 2 team. Thank you for the game and for actually reading feedback. Support (Ari) directed me to post this here because the current Behavior Score system has a fundamental design flaw at the ~3k level. The way the communication ban interacts with automated reports creates an impossible, inescapable loop for players who are genuinely trying to win and improve their score. **The Core Design Flaw: Playing with Bots** Communication is the absolute core of any multiplayer team game. When you completely remove a player's ability to communicate, you turn a team-based strategic game into a single-player experience. I might as well be playing against bots, because the interaction with my team is exactly the same. When you drop below 6,000 behavior score, you cannot ask for help, coordinate with your team, ping the map effectively, or explain macro decisions. Because you cannot explain your actions, teammates lacking map awareness automatically assume you are griefing, report you, and the automated system issues severe punishments with zero human oversight. **Case Study from a Recent Match:** To demonstrate how this algorithm fails, here is exactly what happened in my recent match. I played Axe offlane with a Phoenix support against a very tough Spectre and Enchantress lane. Phoenix was role-abusing, taking farm and last hits instead of helping me survive. From a gameplay design perspective, what is the intended correct play here? - **Option A:** Stand at a safe distance on the lane, get zero gold, and leech experience from my support (who can safely solo the lane due to range and escape skills). This is widely considered griefing. - **Option B:** Leave the unplayable lane, move to the jungle to recover, and let the support have the lane. I chose Option B. I stopped contesting Phoenix for farm and went to jungle. Because I was completely muted by the system, I couldn't tell my team why I was doing this. Here is how the situation escalated: - Phoenix followed me to the jungle to steal last hits from a triple-stacked camp I made. - He/she then moved to the safe lane to stand in trees, doing nothing, but to leech XP from our carries. - He/she went in to bushes to AFK for about 15 seconds from a middle of teamfight with full hp. I ended up doing the supports (Phoenix) work, buying 3 Observers and 6 Sentries, while the actual support bought exactly 2 Sentries in a 42-minute game. I also made several immediate buybacks after dying. Again, because I was muted, I couldn't explain that this was a deliberate macro strategy. Returning to the lane meant instant death from Spectre and Enchantress. Buying back allowed me to farm safer areas and stay close to the game's overall XP progression. The scoreboard at the end of the game proves this strategy worked: I successfully kept up with the level progression and was on the exact same level as everyone else. Once I got the relevant basic items (Vanguard, Blink Dagger to counter the 4 ranged enemies, and a Blade Mail), I rotated back, tanked damage, initiated fights, and we actually won the game. I was even commended by our carries. **The Automated Punishment & The Single Draft Trap:** Despite adapting to a griefing teammate, buying the wards, playing to the very end, and winning the game, the automated system immediately hit me with a 4-hour matchmaking ban, a -500 behavior score drop, and a Low Priority penalty requiring 3 Single Draft wins to escape. This Single Draft penalty is completely contradictory and feeds directly into the same broken loop: - You are forced to play with actual, legitimate griefers who are in Low Priority for the right reasons. - Because the hero pool is restricted, teammates frequently pick unsuitable heroes for the lineup, leading to setups with 4 or 5 hard carries. - People refuse to adapt their roles, or they simply have never played the random heroes they were given. - This inevitably leads to more griefing, ruined games, and consequently, more false reports from tilted teammates. - As a result, your behavior score continues to tank even further based on false reports while you are just trying to win your 3 mandatory matches. I am a 37-year-old man, and I do not believe I have ever been a toxic player. I do not throw rage fits, and I have never abandoned a match midway through unless there was a power outage (which hasn't happened in years). I am a team player—in non-role queue games, if everyone else picks a carry or a tank, I will always try to pick a support or whatever role the team is missing. To be completely honest, I do not even remember why my behavior score originally dropped to ~3000, because it happened several years ago. Description **Request to rework or remove the current Communication/Behavior system in Dota 2** Hello Valve, I would like to ask you to seriously reconsider the current Communication/Behavior system in Dota 2. The problem is that a system designed to reduce toxicity has started to negatively affect one of the most important parts of Dota 2 - communication between teammates. Dota 2 is a team game. Players need to communicate constantly: call missing heroes, suggest objectives, coordinate Roshan, smokes, buybacks, item timings, team fights, lane swaps, defensive actions and dozens of other situations. However, the current system creates an environment where players are increasingly afraid to communicate at all. Players avoid using voice chat, text chat and sometimes even pings because any active interaction with teammates can potentially result in reports and a reduction of Communication Score. As a result, the safest way to protect your account and Behavior Score is simply to remain silent. This creates an absurd situation: **The optimal behavior in a competitive 5v5 team game is to avoid communicating with your team.** The consequences are clearly visible in matchmaking: * players rarely use voice chat; * important information is not communicated; * teammates do not discuss strategy; * players are afraid to criticize even obvious gameplay mistakes; * communication often starts only when the match is already lost; * coordinated play in solo matchmaking becomes significantly harder; * reports can effectively be used as a punishment for disagreement rather than actual toxic behavior. There is also an important distinction between **toxicity** and **communication that another player simply does not like**. Insults, harassment, racism, threats and intentional spam should obviously be punishable. But saying things such as: "Don't fight without buyback." "Please stop farming and come Roshan." "We need BKB before the next fight." "Don't go high ground now." "Can you TP bottom?" should not create a risk for a player's ability to communicate in future matches simply because another player disagreed with the call and decided to report them. The current system incentivizes silence instead of healthy team communication. I believe Valve should either substantially redesign this system or remove the communication restrictions in their current form. Possible improvements could include: 1. Separate actual toxic behavior from ordinary gameplay communication and disagreements. 2. Reduce the influence of mass communication reports when there is no evidence of abusive behavior. 3. Make Communication Score penalties more transparent so players understand exactly what behavior resulted in a restriction. 4. Do not remove essential team communication tools from players unless there is clear evidence of serious or repeated abuse. 5. Introduce stronger protection against report abuse after lost matches. 6. Evaluate the content and context of communication instead of relying primarily on the number of reports. 7. Preserve essential strategic communication such as voice, pings and gameplay calls wherever possible. Dota 2 is one of the most complex competitive team games ever created. Communication should be encouraged, not treated as a potential risk to the player's account. A system intended to combat toxicity should punish toxic behavior. It should not make silence the safest strategy. Please consider reviewing the current Communication/Behavior system and its impact on actual teamwork in matchmaking. Thank you. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No Description There is a critical logical flaw in the automated Behavior Score system that causes a permanent soft-lock for solo queue players trapped below 3000 score. For the past 6 months, my account has been completely restricted from ranked matchmaking, voice chat, and text chat. Despite being physically unable to commit any communication abuse (due to the permanent system mute), my behavior score continues to drop or remains frozen at the absolute bottom. The automated system aggregates all reports blindly without assessing context. In low behavior brackets, solo queue players are constantly matched with pre-made party stacks (2, 3, or 4 players). When a party loses a match, they subjectively use the silent solo player as a scapegoat, issuing 3 to 4 reports simultaneously out of spite. The system treats this mass party report as a consensus of toxic behavior. This creates an inescapable mathematical deadlock: 1. To increase the behavior score, a player must play standard matches. 2. Playing standard matches as a solo queue player naturally triggers false, subjective reports from toxic party stacks. 3. The automated system accepts these reports (even for communication abuse on a completely muted account), lowering the score even further. Currently, the only way to escape this automated prison is to break Steam's ToS by paying third-party boosting services to play in a 5-man stack where reports are impossible. This is a technical system loop that cannot be resolved automatically. I kindly request a developer or technical administrator to review my account logs for the past 6 months, verify that I have not committed any genuine griefing (destroying items, running down mid), and manually adjust or reset my behavior score to a baseline level. Description The current Communication/Behavior Score system and its automated in-game mutes are actively hurting the matchmaking experience. Dota 2 is a highly competitive, team-oriented game that requires constant communication. The problems with the current mute system are: 1. System Abuse: The automated mute system is easily abused. Players frequently use communication reports to punish teammates for bad gameplay (missed spells, lost lanes), rather than actual toxicity. 2. Collateral Damage: A globally muted player cannot coordinate with their team (calling missing, Roshan timings, smoke ganks). This essentially punishes the 4 other innocent players on the team who are now playing at a severe disadvantage. 3. Impossible to Recover: Once a player's communication score drops, it is incredibly difficult to raise it back up because they cannot communicate to be commended, creating a vicious cycle. Suggested changes to rework the system: - Replace the forced absolute mute with a "soft mute". By default, the player is muted, but teammates should have a clear button to manually UNMUTE them if they want to coordinate. - Do not restrict essential gameplay pings and basic chat wheel commands for muted players. - Rework the automated penalty system so that report volume alone doesn't trigger immediate, severe communication bans without actual text/voice chat analysis. Please reconsider how this system operates, as it currently causes more frustration than it prevents. 4. Encouraging Griefing: The sudden in-game mute often demoralizes the team and triggers griefing behavior. For instance, in a recent match, immediately after a player received a system mute mid-game, two other teammates simply gave up and stopped playing entirely. is a long-standing and very frustrating issue in Dota 2 related to the communication system and the Behavior Score system. When a player has a low behavior score, is in low priority, or is in a muted/punished chat pool (due to reports), the in-game chat becomes restricted or disabled. As a result, the /roll command (which generates a random number to resolve disputes) stops working in all modes, including normal non-role queue matches (All Pick without strict role assignment). What this leads to: Draft Chaos. When two players both want to play mid (or carry/offlane), they have no fair way to decide who gets the role. Double Mid Syndrome. Since /roll is unavailable, players just lock a second mid hero anyway, turning the game into a toxic mess from minute zero. Game Ruining. Instead of a civilized resolution, arguments escalate, players start flaming each other, and often intentionally feed or grief because the dispute is only resolved by "who picks faster". Inequality. This issue disproportionately affects players with low behavior scores — who are already in a bad spot. Instead of giving them tools to resolve conflicts peacefully (like rolling), the system takes that tool away, making matches even more unbearable and preventing them from recovering their score. The Core Problem: /roll is NOT a social chat message; it is a gameplay mechanic (a console/chat command) that returns a random integer. Muting chat or restricting communication should not affect gameplay commands, especially in non-role queue modes where /roll is the only civilized way to distribute roles. Proposed Solution: Make the /roll command available regardless of "Low Priority", "Muted", or "Low Behavior Score" status. Alternatively, add a "Roll" button directly to the hero selection UI that is always functional (similar to how it works in tournament/captain's mode drafts or custom lobbies). This is a critical quality-of-life improvement for the community that would significantly reduce toxicity and the number of ruined Dota 2 developers and community, I would like to ask for clarification regarding the current Behavior Score and Communication Score system. My current scores are: Behavior Score: 12,000 / 12,000 (maximum) Communication Score: 5,800 / 12,000 I regularly play Dota 2 and I do not intentionally grief, feed, destroy my items, abandon matches, throw games, or smurf. In ranked games, I play the roles assigned to me by the matchmaking system and try to play for the win. I also support Dota 2 financially and enjoy the game, which is why I would like to understand how this system works and how it could potentially be improved. I recently checked my Steam Personal Game Data → Dota 2 → Account → Incoming Match Player Report. My recent data shows Communication Reports even during periods where I had no abandons or excessive reports. For example: August 11: - 15 matches - 15 positive matches - 0 reported matches - 0 abandons - 3 Communication Reports from 2 reporting parties August 8: - 15 matches - 14 positive matches - 1 reported match - 0 abandons - 4 Communication Reports from 3 reporting parties August 6: - 15 matches - 11 positive matches - 4 reported matches - 0 abandons - 7 total reports - 4 Communication Reports from 4 reporting parties August 2: - 15 matches - 15 positive matches - 0 reported matches - 0 abandons - 0 Communication Reports My main question is: How can a player have a maximum Behavior Score of 12,000/12,000 while having a Communication Score of only 5,800/12,000? I understand that these are separate systems and that Communication Reports can affect Communication Score. However, I am concerned about the possibility of unjustified or retaliatory reports. There is another situation that I believe is worth considering. In a five-player team, it is possible that three players are in the same party and know each other. If one of these players has a disagreement with me, the other two party members may potentially report me simply to support their friend, even if they did not personally witness any actual communication violation. In this situation, what could start as a disagreement between two players could potentially result in multiple reports against the same player simply because several players are grouped together. For example, instead of receiving one report from the player involved in the disagreement, I could potentially receive reports from all three members of the party because they want to support their friend. This raises an important question: Does the Communication Score system take party relationships or coordinated/retaliatory reporting into account? If multiple members of the same party report the same player, are these reports treated completely independently, or does the system recognize that they may be related to the same incident? I believe this is important because otherwise a single conflict between two players could potentially have a disproportionately large effect on another player's Communication Score. Players can report each other because of disagreements, frustration after losing a game, disagreements about gameplay decisions, or personal conflicts. Therefore, I would like to understand how the system prevents abuse of Communication Reports. I contacted Steam Support about this issue. They told me that the scores are automated and that Steam Support cannot manually adjust them. They also stated that they do not provide additional information about how the behavior scoring system is calculated. They recommended that I bring this issue to the Dota 2 community and development forums. So this is what I am doing. I am NOT asking for my Communication Score to be manually increased. I would simply like to understand whether the current system can incorrectly penalize a player because of unjustified, retaliatory, or potentially coordinated Communication Reports, and whether there are mechanisms that prevent players from abusing the reporting system. I would also like to raise another question regarding the recovery of Communication Score. Why does the Communication Score not have some form of regular recalibration or review period, for example once a year? Would it be possible to introduce an annual recalibration, review, or another mechanism that would give players who have demonstrated consistently good behavior over a long period of time a clearer way to recover their Communication Score? In my subjective opinion, there appears to be a significant imbalance between losing Communication Score and recovering it. It feels like a player can receive Communication Reports relatively easily and potentially lose Communication Score very quickly, while recovering that lost score through consistently good behavior appears to be much slower. Even if a player makes a serious effort to communicate politely and avoid violations over a long period of time, recovering from a low Communication Score can feel extremely difficult. In other words, the negative effect of reports can appear very quickly, while the positive effect of consistently good behavior takes much longer to become visible. I believe that a regular recalibration or another transparent recovery mechanism could make the system feel more fair. It would also give players a clearer motivation to improve their behavior because they would know that consistently good behavior over time can meaningfully restore their Communication Score. If there is no way for players to verify whether reports against them were legitimate, how can they know what behavior they need to change? I would appreciate any clarification from the Dota 2 developers or experienced players who understand how the current system works. I am not asking for special treatment for my account. I am asking whether the current system could be improved to make Communication Score more resistant to report abuse and to provide players with a reasonable path to recover from a low score through consistently good behavior. Description Title: Feedback / Suggestion: Behavior Score system needs real-time updating and better balance for isolated bad games Body: Hi Valve team, I’d like to share some feedback regarding the current Behavior & Communication Score system. Currently, receiving a summary every 15 games makes the system feel rigid and unfair. A player can play 14 great games, have 1 bad game (or get targeted by a toxic party/tilted teammates), and end up with a heavily penalized report or even low priority. One single bad match shouldn't outweigh two weeks of good behavior. Suggestions for improvement: Real-time updates (similar to modern mobile competitive games): Instead of waiting 15 games for a batch update, let every single match influence the score dynamically. Weighted Recency: Recent games should hold meaningful weight, but isolated incidents shouldn't drastically ruin an entire reporting period. Better Variance Protection: A single bad game out of 15 should be treated as an anomaly, not a trend. This change would make the system feel much more transparent, fair, and encouraging for players who are actively trying to maintain high behavior scores. Description ### Summary The current report and communication score system in Dota 2 feels too passive. Bad actors can severely insult opponents in All-Chat, ruin everyone's emotional state, and they only receive a minor score deduction matches later. We need a firmer, faster, and more transparent approach to protect the player base from toxicity. ### Why we need this (Balancing Environment and Player Retention) We understand that Valve needs to maintain its player base. Permanently banning or suspending accounts for chat toxicity can be counterproductive, as it drives players away entirely and ruins matchmaking times. Instead of banning the account, we should strictly "strip away their ability to ruin the game environment" while still letting them play the game. Keeping them in the game but forcing them into silence is the perfect balance for player retention and community health. ### Proposed Solutions 1. **Immediate All-Chat Time-out (Real-time Mitigation):** If the system detects severe toxic keywords or verified report spikes in All-Chat, that player should be instantly and automatically muted from All-Chat for the rest of the match or the next 24 hours. Stop the toxicity in its tracks before it spreads to other players. 2. **100% Automated System Reading (No Human Check Needed):** The system should automatically scan all chat logs using a pre-defined blocklist of toxic words, slurs, and toxic gaming jargon (e.g., "ez", "noob", "trash", "dog", etc.). There is no need for manual human checkers. If the text matches the filter, the penalty is executed immediately by the server. 3. **The "First-Striker" Principle (Protecting Those Who Reply):** Often, a toxic player starts the insults, and their teammates or opponents only reply out of frustration. The system should only punish the **first person** who initiates the toxic behavior in that specific chat timeline. Anyone who replies or defends themselves afterwards should NOT be penalized. Punishing the "first striker" stops the root cause of the toxicity without unfairly striking back at victims who are just reacting to provocation. 4. **Heavier Penalties for Severe Insults (-2000 Score):** Ruinous behavior shouldn't cost just 100 points. Severe toxic words should trigger a massive, immediate deduction (e.g., -2000 communication score). Since players lose All-Chat privileges when dropping below 10,000 points, one single toxic outburst should instantly silence them for dozens of matches until they earn it back. 5. **Transparency (Show the Evidence Log):** When players lose score, the client should show them a notification displaying exactly which log/words triggered the penalty. They need to know precisely *what* they typed that led to the punishment. Winning a game shouldn't be an excuse to demean opponents. Respecting the enemy team is basic sportsmanship, and Valve can enforce it strictly through precise, heavy chat restrictions without having to ban players from playing. ### Example Match ID (and Description ​The current Behavior Score system is detrimental to the Dota 2 experience. It fails to distinguish between unavoidable technical issues (power/internet outages, hardware failures) and intentional disruptive behavior. As a result, players are trapped in a "point of no return," where recovery is nearly impossible. ​The game is fundamentally a team-based experience, yet this system forces players into a state of "silent survival." Players are now terrified to use voice or text chat to coordinate, as any interaction can trigger retaliatory reports from teammates. This silence destroys the core of Dota 2, as communication is essential for team play. ​Furthermore, this system drives players to abandon their main accounts and create new ones, which devalues the competitive integrity of the game. ​Proposed Reforms: ​Remove the Hidden Behavior Score: Replace the current hidden point system with a transparent and predictable disciplinary model. ​Clear Penalties for Abandoning: Instead of a complex score reduction, implement direct consequences for technical issues. For example: 3 abandons = 5 games of Low Priority. ​Targeted Communication Bans: If a player receives reports from all 9 other players in a single match, they should receive a 48-hour communication ban. If the behavior persists, the punishment should escalate to Low Priority matches without access to chat for the purpose of "correction." ​Low Priority Revamp: Replace the mandatory "Single Draft" (SD) mode in Low Priority with "All Random" (AR). This makes the punishment less monotonous and keeps the game engaging, even for those serving time. ​Address Report Abuse and the Overwatch System: The current report system is heavily abused as a weapon against teammates. Furthermore, the "Overwatch" system is ineffective because reviewers often lack context or are biased, leading to unfair judgments. We need a system that filters out malicious, weaponized reports rather than penalizing any form of communication. ​The goal should be to encourage positive communication and team play, not to force players into "mute mode" or drive them away from the game entirely. I urge the development team to reconsider the current model in favor of a more transparent and fair disciplinary framework. I'd like to suggest a possible improvement to the current Behavior Score and Communication Score system. I wanted to share some feedback about the current Behavior Score and Communication Score system in Dota 2. The system has been in the game for almost three years now, and I think it has one major problem: once a player drops to a very low Behavior Score, it's extremely difficult to recover. You can play many games without abandoning or griefing and still gain only a small amount of Behavior Score. At the same time, it's very easy to lose hundreds of points from reports. Sometimes it feels like simply using chat is enough to get reported, even if you're just trying to communicate with your team. Because of this, many players can't use voice and text chat altogether. Others create new accounts just so they can play normally again, communicate with teammates, and queue for Ranked. I don't think that's the goal of the system. I think it would be worth considering some kind of amnesty or reset after all this time. Here are a few possible ideas: * Restore every account that isn't permanently banned to 12,000 Behavior Score and Communication Score. * If a full reset is too much, raise everyone below a certain threshold (for example, 8,000) to a healthier level. * Make Behavior Score recover much faster for players below 8,000, so they have a realistic chance to climb back. * Reduce Behavior Score losses from reports unless those reports are confirmed by the system. * Consider a one-time recovery event for long-term active players who haven't abandoned games or received confirmed griefing penalties for a long period. The system has already been in place for nearly three years. By now, players who wanted to improve their behavior have had plenty of time to do so. A one-time reset would give those players a fair chance to start over, while players who continue to be toxic would naturally lose their score again. The reason I'm suggesting this is simple. Right now, players with low Behavior Score often feel stuck. They can spend weeks trying to improve it and make almost no progress, while losing hundreds of points again after just a few matches. It becomes frustrating enough that many people simply stop playing on their main account. I also believe this would reduce the number of new accounts being created. Right now, many players feel that creating a new account is much easier than trying to recover their main account, and that's probably not the outcome the system was designed to encourage. I believe giving players another chance after almost three years would improve communication, reduce the number of new accounts being created, and make the system feel much fairer. Players who continue to be toxic would naturally lose their Behavior Score again, so the purpose of the system would remain the same. I really enjoy Dota 2, and I'm only writing this because I think this change would make the game better for a lot of players. Thank you for your time. I'd also like to hear what other players think. Have you had a similar experience with recovering Behavior Score? Description When a player activates Smoke of Deceit, the in-game notification that appears in team chat ("[Player] used Smoke of Deceit" / smoke activation message) is being treated by the report system as a personal text-chat message sent by that player. Because of this, other players can report me for communication abuse (text chat / voice toxicity) based solely on the automated smoke notification — even though I have no access to text chat or voice communication at all. My communication is restricted (Communication Score: 5200), and I have never sent a chat message or used voice in these games. This is critical: in Dota, a communication report can only be submitted for voice toxicity or text-chat toxicity. Game-ruining behavior is tracked under a separate, general "Reports" metric (see column 10 in the attached statistics). The reports I am receiving are landing under the communication category (column 12) — which is logically impossible, because I have no communication access for which I could be reported. Timeline proving the bug The correlation is exact: toxicity reports against me started immediately after the Smoke update was released, even though I have never had chat access during that period. My text chat was only unlocked for a single short window: from 2026-06-05 13:46:59 GMT to 2026-06-08 17:43:51 GMT. Outside of that window, my Behavior Score was below 6,000, so chat/communication was locked entirely. Despite chat being locked, the communication reports kept coming in — coinciding precisely with matches in which I activated Smoke of Deceit. This confirms the smoke notification is being misattributed as my own communication. Match ID Matches for analysis: 8846190591 8846133477 8845268767 Timestamp when the bug occurs The issue triggers at the moment Smoke of Deceit is activated and the team-chat notification appears. See the timestamps of the smoke activations in the matches listed above. Steps to reproduce Use an account with text/voice communication restricted (Behavior Score below the communication threshold, no chat access). Enter a match and activate Smoke of Deceit. Observe the smoke-activation notification appearing in team chat. After the match, have another player submit a "communication abuse / text chat" report against the smoking player. The report is accepted and applied as a communication offense (column 12), despite the player having no chat or voice access and having sent no actual messages. Description Subject: Request for Behavior Score Review or Guidance Dear Valve Corporation / Dota 2 Support Team, I have been playing Dota 2 for many years, and I am currently facing ongoing difficulties in improving my behavior score, despite maintaining a consistent and respectful attitude during matches. I primarily play as a hard carry and always focus on winning. In difficult games, especially when teammates are underperforming or engaging in constant, unfavorable fights, I choose to prioritize farming and avoid unnecessary deaths. My goal is to build enough resources to defend the high ground and potentially turn the game around, rather than participating in fights that are clearly lost. However, this approach often leads to frustration among teammates. In many cases, they begin to question my decisions, follow me, or even intentionally disrupt my gameplay. Despite this, I remain respectful, commend teammates when appropriate, report only clear cases of disruptive behavior, and often commend opponents as well. Even with this consistent conduct, I continue to receive reports, which causes my behavior score to remain low or decrease further. It feels like I am stuck in a negative cycle, where disruptive players report each other and prevent real progress for those trying to improve. Because of this, I would like to ask: Is there any possibility of reviewing or resetting my behavior score? Or is there any official method or guidance to recover it fairly under these circumstances? I also believe that a periodic reset system (similar to MMR recalibration) could help players who have improved their behavior demonstrate that change over time. Thank you for your time and attention. Valve Support / Dota 2 Team, I’m writing to report a recurring problem with Dota 2’s reporting and Conduct Summary system that is negatively affecting my account’s Communication and Behavior scores. Problem summary I primarily play as a duo with a friend. In about half of our games we are matched with a group of three (trio) on the other team. Frequently those opposing trios grief and then report my friend and me together, even when we have not done anything to deserve a report. Because multiple players from the same party submit reports, our accounts receive multiple reports in a single match (often three reports each), which appears to disproportionately affect our Communication and Behavior scores. As a result, our communication score has dropped significantly and we’re finding it extremely difficult to recover it despite playing consistently and not engaging in the behaviors cited. This feels unfair because coordinated reporting by parties of friends can be used to punish other players without valid cause. Why this is a problem It encourages misuse of the reporting system by coordinated groups. It penalizes players who are not at fault and makes it hard to restore reputation. The current system does not appear to account for context (matched parties, retaliation, or false reporting by the same party across matches). Suggested fixes / requests Consider implementing weighting or de-duplication of reports from the same party in a single match (e.g., treat reports from multiple players in the same party as a single report for scoring purposes). Add better transparency in Conduct summaries about why specific penalties or score drops occurred, including when multiple reports from the same party were a factor. Provide a clearer, faster appeals path or manual review for players who believe they were falsely or unfairly reported due to coordinated griefing/retaliation. Improve heuristics to detect coordinated false-reporting patterns across matches and discount or flag them. Supporting details My Steam ID / account: ibra_malallah / 76561198291661601 Please let me know if you need more information. Description Description We, representatives of the CIS Dota 2 community, as well as, in essence, a significant portion of the global Dota 2 player base, would like to formally express our deep concern regarding the current state of the game and its direction in recent years. Dota 2 has long been more than just a game for us - it is a competitive environment, a community, and a cultural phenomenon. However, many long-standing issues continue to negatively impact the player experience, and we believe they are not receiving the attention they deserve. Behavior Score System The current behavior score system is widely perceived as ineffective and, in many cases, unnecessary. Instead of improving match quality, it often creates frustration and imbalance. The system discourages communication between players, lacks fairness, and at times does not accurately reflect actual in-game behavior. As a result, it reduces overall enjoyment of the game. Ranked System The ranking system raises serious concerns. The gap between skill levels and MMR brackets is extremely large, making progression disproportionately difficult and time-consuming. For many players, ranking up requires an unrealistic investment of time, which reduces long-term engagement and motivation. Cheating and Fair Play One of the most critical issues is the growing presence of cheaters in public matches. This problem severely undermines competitive integrity. Many players believe that anti-cheat measures are insufficient and that enforcement actions are nearly nonexistent. A stronger and more transparent stance on fair play is urgently needed. Quality of Updates Recent updates are perceived as lacking depth, coherence, and clear direction. Changes often feel unfinished or disconnected from the needs of the community. This creates the impression that development is no longer guided by a clear vision for the game. Gameplay and Balance There is growing concern regarding the current gameplay direction and overall balance of the game. The meta is heavily dominated by aura-based items, which reduces strategic diversity and limits viable playstyles. Matches have shifted away from dynamic teamfights toward prolonged farming, making gameplay feel slower and less engaging. Additionally, the current comeback mechanics often lead to excessively long games, even in situations where one team has a clear advantage. Overall, there is a strong ощущение that player feedback is not being adequately considered, and that balance decisions are disconnected from the community’s expectations. Lack of Meaningful Events Over the past year, there has been a noticeable absence of engaging and memorable in-game events. Historically, events have played a key role in maintaining player interest and community enthusiasm. Their decline has led to a significant drop in overall engagement. Technical Issues, Bugs, and Server Stability There is growing concern regarding the overall technical condition of the game. Players frequently encounter bugs that remain unresolved for extended periods of time. In addition, server instability has become a recurring issue - matches can suffer from severe lag, sometimes lasting 30 minutes or more, directly impacting game outcomes and ruining the competitive experience. Furthermore, numerous visual and interface-related bugs reduce usability, negatively affecting play. Taken together, these issues create the impression of insufficient attention to the technical quality of the game. We are writing this not out of negativity, but out of genuine concern for the future of Dota 2. We believe in the game’s potential and its legacy, and we hope to see it thrive once again. We strongly urge greater transparency, closer communication with the community, and decisive action on the issues outlined above. I would like to share some observations about the current Behavior Score and communication restriction system in Dota 2. I have been playing Dota since the Dota Allstars era (around 2004) and was also active during the time of dota-league.com, one of the earlier community platforms that already implemented matchmaking, reporting systems, and moderation. Having played the game for more than 20 years with very few breaks, I have followed the evolution of its systems quite closely. This post is not meant as a complaint, but rather as long-term player feedback about some interactions in the current system that may produce unintended effects on player behavior and match quality. Dota 2 relies heavily on coordination and information exchange between players. During matches, players often need to communicate things such as ultimate cooldowns, teleport cooldowns, buyback availability, or the need to delay a fight until certain abilities are available. These kinds of details can strongly influence the outcome of fights and objectives. When players receive communication restrictions due to Behavior Score penalties, it becomes difficult to communicate this type of information. As a result, teammates may misinterpret certain decisions during a match. For example, a player might not join a fight because abilities are on cooldown, because the engagement is clearly lost, or because positioning or farming for the next objective is the safer decision. Without communication, these decisions can easily appear as intentional non-cooperation. Reports are typically submitted during or immediately after matches. At that point, it may not yet be clear whether a decision that appeared questionable during the game was actually strategically correct. For instance, refusing to follow a teammate into a lost engagement may look negative in the moment but can later turn out to be the correct macro decision for the team. Because reports happen immediately, they can sometimes reflect frustration in the moment rather than an objective evaluation of behavior. When communication is limited, players also cannot explain their reasoning during the match. This may increase misunderstandings and lead to additional reports. I understand that Valve likely uses background systems to evaluate report accuracy over time, but restricted communication may still contribute to a feedback loop where misunderstandings increase reports and reports further reduce communication. From earlier community-run systems such as dota-league.com, reporting mechanisms also existed. Those systems were simpler and largely player-driven, but they often focused on clearly disruptive behavior. They also included moderation steps such as report reviews, cooldowns, temporary bans, and bans for multi-accounting to prevent players from bypassing penalties. While the system itself was simpler, enforcement against multi-accounting made it harder to circumvent the intended penalties. In the current environment, creating new accounts is relatively easy. While I understand that Dota 2 already has safeguards such as restricting ranked access for new accounts and estimating player skill before calibration matches, multi-accounting can still occur. Experienced players creating additional accounts can result in skill imbalances in matches. This may cause frustration among teammates and indirectly lead to toxicity or reports even when the underlying cause is the match imbalance rather than individual behavior. Another observation that may indicate unintended incentives relates to Low Priority Single Draft matches. Interestingly, some players report that these matches can sometimes feel less tense or less toxic than normal ranked games, even though they are intended as a penalty environment. From personal experience, I sometimes find Low Priority Single Draft games more enjoyable than regular ranked games, which seems paradoxical. I also know players who intentionally try to receive reports in order to play in Low Priority because they perceive those matches as less stressful than the normal Single Draft queue. If players intentionally attempt to enter Low Priority to access a different match environment, this may suggest that the system is producing unintended incentives. At the same time, intentionally steering accounts into Low Priority may further distort matchmaking and player behavior. Over the many years I have played Dota, it felt at certain points that the overall match environment was more balanced and less toxic. As someone who has followed the game for more than two decades, I find some of these developments unfortunate and would simply appreciate if this type of long-term player feedback could be considered during future improvements to the behavior and reporting systems. Description Hi, I want to give real feedback about the Behavior Score system, because honestly it feels broken and unfair. In my recent match, two of my teammates started watching everything I did and criticizing every move I made. They were constantly commenting on where I go, what items I build, why I’m on this lane, why I’m not grouping — basically judging every decision I made. At the same time, they were making mistakes themselves and dying for no reason. Because of that, I started responding and explaining what I was doing. I explained that I was split pushing, controlling lanes, creating pressure, and playing the map the way my hero is supposed to. I also started making calls — telling when to back, when not to fight, when to reset, and how we could stabilize the game. I also pointed out their mistakes, like when they went mid and died for nothing after objectives were already gone. I wasn’t trying to attack them, I was trying to explain the situation and help us win. Some teammates actually started listening to my calls. Others kept insulting me and blaming me. But I kept playing, kept calling, and kept focusing on winning. Eventually, even during fights and arguments, the team followed the path and calls I was making. My strategy worked, and we won the game. But during the conflict, I received a chat restriction. And after the match, I received a 4-hour matchmaking ban and lost around 1000 Behavior Score. This is the main problem. It feels like if you speak, communicate, and try to lead, you become a target. People get angry, they blame you, they report you, and the system punishes you automatically without understanding what actually happened. This has happened more than once. Whenever I try to communicate, make calls, ping objectives, or help coordinate the team, I become the most visible person, and frustrated teammates use reports against me. So the system basically teaches you one thing: don’t talk, don’t communicate, don’t try to lead. Just stay silent if you want to protect your Behavior Score. But Dota 2 is a team game. Communication should be encouraged, not punished. And this is not just my personal problem. This issue is widespread in the community. Many large YouTube creators have talked about the Behavior Score system and its problems. Videos discussing this topic have hundreds of thousands of views and tens of thousands of likes. There are entire discussions and videos dedicated to how frustrating and unfair this system feels for players who try to communicate and lead. Right now it feels like the system punishes players who try to play properly and help their team, simply because other players get emotional and use reports as a weapon. I hope you can seriously review and improve this system, because right now it discourages teamwork instead of supporting it. Description Адресат: Valve / команда разработки Dota 2 Настоящим мы обращаемся с требованием полного удаления системы Communication Score из Dota 2 как системно неисправной и наносящей прямой вред качеству игры. Данный вывод сделан не на основании единичного инцидента, а по итогам многолетнего использования системы и массовой реакции игрового сообщества. За годы существования Communication Score на форуме Steam были созданы тысячи тем, в которых игроки независимо друг от друга описывают одни и те же проблемы: непрозрачность, непредсказуемость наказаний и отсутствие реального пути восстановления. Ключевые проблемы системы Отсутствие проверки содержания коммуникации Система опирается на репорты, которые не проходят валидацию по содержанию. Она не различает токсичное поведение, активную игровую коммуникацию и просто обильное общение. В результате наказываются не только токсичные игроки, но и: новички, активно задающие вопросы; лидеры, дающие коллы и координирующие команду; любые «заметные» игроки, чаще взаимодействующие с командой. Непрозрачный и нестабильный вес репортов Репорты имеют неочевидный и непредсказуемый вес. В одних случаях несколько репортов не приводят к заметным последствиям, в других — один репорт способен вызвать резкое падение Communication Score (сотни или тысячи очков) без объяснения причин. Это делает систему недоверяемой и невоспроизводимой. Наказания без причинно-следственной связи На практике фиксируются случаи, когда репорты от игроков вражеской команды применяются даже при отсутствии токсичной коммуникации. Репорт может быть следствием поражения и эмоциональной реакции, но система не отличает такие ситуации от реальных нарушений. Отсутствие работающего механизма восстановления Даже при сотнях матчей, положительной статистике, минимальном количестве репортов и большом числе лайков Communication Score может: не расти месяцами; обрушиваться за несколько игр без объяснимых причин. Это означает, что система не имеет корректного «конечного состояния выхода» из наказания. Критический ущерб командной игре и соревновательной целостности Автоматические мьюты: напрямую ухудшают качество матчей; лишают команды координации; влияют на исходы побед и поражений. Особенно критично это в premade-группах. Игроки объединяются в группы именно для командной игры и координации. Любые автоматические ограничения общения в таких условиях противоречат самой цели групповой игры и наносят максимальный ущерб. Избыточность системы В Dota 2 уже существуют достаточные и эффективные инструменты индивидуальной фильтрации: mute, ignore, отключение чата и голосовой связи. Эти инструменты позволяют каждому игроку самостоятельно решать, кого он хочет слышать, не нарушая симметрию матчей и не ограничивая остальных. Communication Score не добавляет новой ценности и дублирует функции, уже реализованные более корректно. Деградация коммуникационной среды за годы использования За более чем три года существования Communication Score: токсичность в игре не была устранена; при этом нормальная, полезная командная коммуникация практически исчезла. Игроки массово предпочитают молчать из страха получить репорт, даже когда общение повышает шансы на победу. Это подтверждается как личным опытом, так и тысячами обсуждений на официальном форуме Steam. Description Addressee: Valve / Dota 2 Development Team We hereby request the complete removal of the Communication Score system from Dota 2 as a fundamentally flawed system that causes direct harm to match quality. This conclusion is not based on an isolated incident. It is the result of years of real-world use and extensive community feedback. Over the lifetime of Communication Score, thousands of forum threads have been created on Steam, consistently describing the same issues: lack of transparency, unpredictable penalties, and the absence of a reliable recovery mechanism. Core issues No validation of communication content The system relies on reports without validating the actual content of communication. It does not distinguish between toxicity, active gameplay coordination, and frequent but neutral communication. As a result, it punishes: new players asking questions, team leaders making calls, any highly visible or communicative player. Opaque and inconsistent report weighting Reports have an unclear and inconsistent impact. Multiple reports may have little effect, while in other cases a single report can cause a massive score drop without explanation. This makes the system non-transparent and unreliable. Punishment without causal connection Reports from opposing players can be applied even when no toxic communication occurred. Emotion-driven reports after a loss are not filtered or distinguished from legitimate cases. No functional recovery path Even after hundreds of matches with positive behavior, minimal reports, and many commendations, the Communication Score may: stagnate indefinitely; collapse within a few matches. This indicates the absence of a valid recovery endpoint. Direct damage to competitive integrity Automatic mutes: reduce match quality, break team coordination, directly affect win and loss outcomes. This is especially damaging in premade groups, where communication is the primary reason players group up. Any automatic communication restriction in such cases contradicts the purpose of team play. System redundancy Dota 2 already provides effective individual filtering tools such as mute and ignore. These tools allow players to manage their own experience without breaking match symmetry. Communication Score adds no unique value. Long-term degradation of communication After more than three years of use: toxicity has not been eliminated, meaningful team communication has largely disappeared. Players increasingly choose silence out of fear of reports, even when communication would improve gameplay. This trend is widely documented across the Steam community. Request For the reasons stated above, we request the complete removal of the Communication Score system from Dota 2 as a system that is: structurally irreparable, opaque and unpredictable, redundant, status** Complete silence and ignoring from Valve **What became clear after the discussion** Based on the discussion in this thread, the analysis of other topics, and publicly available information, it became obvious that the problem is not about isolated "edge cases" or specific numbers. This is about the system logic itself and its impact on teamplay . In its current implementation, Communication Score in the long run is primarily driven by report and mute statistics , not by the actual quality or context of communication. At the same time, text and voice analysis is mostly used for fast punishments (mutes) , but it does not solve the problem of cumulative score degradation . **Why staying silent does not protect you** Silence is not a protection, because the "Politeness" score can decrease even when there is no communication at all . This means a complete absence of any interaction: no pings, no voice chat, no text messages . By design, the "Politeness" metric is supposed to reflect the quality of communication . In practice, however, it can change without any communication happening . In other words, a metric tied to communication continues to drop even when communication does not exist. **Main problem: the system breaks teamplay** The core issue is that the system restricts communication without addressing the root causes of conflicts. When the score drops, a player loses the ability to interact properly with the team, while still being placed into matches where communication is critically important . In Dota, communication is not a bonus or a "nice-to-have feature". It is the foundation of team-based gameplay . Calls, timings, cooldown information, and positioning directly affect fights and match outcomes. When part of the team is restricted, the match loses symmetry of conditions , and overall match quality degrades for everyone. In practice it looks like this: you see an opportunity for coordinated action, but due to restrictions you cannot call a timing or request support. Coordination is replaced by guessing and randomness . Even with high "politeness" values, some players remain restricted, while others avoid active communication because of fear of reports . As a result, communication becomes one-sided or disappears completely. **What I propose to discuss in this thread** The real question is no longer about how to "recover" or "farm" politeness score. The question is: why does the game have a system that in its current form does not improve behavior , but instead limits a core gameplay tool and reduces match quality . My assumption is that this system was introduced to increase retention and inflate online numbers. Players tolerated it for several years. That patience is gone. **I propose to focus the discussion on this: the system logic , its transparency , and its impact on the match as a whole . And whether it should be fundamentally reworked or ##disabled. То есть показатель, связанный исключительно с общением, может продолжить снижаться даже тогда, когда общения просто не существует. **Главная проблема: система ломает командную игру** Ключевая проблема в том, что система ограничивает коммуникацию , не устраняя первопричины конфликтов. Description this is what ai said about your stupid broken system Dota 2's behavior system is widely considered "broken" by players because it creates toxic matchmaking trenches, disproportionately punishes good players through malicious reports (especially in lower tiers), struggles to differentiate genuine griefing from disagreements or off-meta plays, and heavily penalizes communication/abandonments more than it rewards positive behavior, leading to frustratingly low scores and unfair match quality. Key issues include unlimited reports, the impact of reports in casual games (like Turbo) affecting Ranked, and an inability to climb out of low-score pools once there. Core Problems with the Behavior Score System: Abuse of Reports: Players can report teammates for minor infractions (losing roll, missing spells, bad plays), and these reports count heavily, even if unverified by Overwatch. The "Trench" Effect: Lower behavior scores lead to more reports from other low-score players, creating a cycle where it's extremely hard to climb out, even with good behavior. Disproportionate Penalties: A few bad games (or even just power outages/bad internet) can tank a score, while regaining points through commends or positive games is slow and difficult. Unfair Punishment for Communication: The Communication Score (Comms Score) is highly sensitive; arguments or frustration in 15% of games can drop it significantly, forcing mutes and hindering team play, while positive play yields few points. Lack of Differentiation: Reports from Turbo (casual) games carry the same weight as Ranked, leading to casual abuse. System Imbalance: Reports and abandons often feel weighted far more heavily than commends, making positive actions insufficient to offset negatives. Player Experiences & Frustrations: Players report losing thousands of points for technical issues or bad luck, feeling unfairly punished for issues beyond their control. Good players get stuck in low-score pools with genuinely toxic players (feeders, intentional griefers) because the system segregates them. Many feel the system doesn't encourage improvement but rather punishes mistakes or perceived lack of meta adherence. In essence, while intended to isolate toxic players, the current behavior system often punishes good players who have bad luck, experience technical issues, or get caught in cycles of malicious Description My behavior score has stayed at the maximum (12,000) with only one report in over 45 matches, yet my **communication score dropped from ~12,000 to 11,089**. I have **not used voice or text chat** in the last week, and have received **dozens of commendations** instead. This seems to indicate that the communication score system is triggering penalties even when no communication is made. ### 🧠 Expected Behavior If a player does not communicate (or communicates positively) and receives no reports, the communication score should remain stable or increase — not decrease. ### 💬 Suggestion Valve should review the detection rules for “communication activity” and consider: - Ignoring “muted by peers” if no text/voice was sent. - Avoiding penalties for inactivity in chat. - Decoupling player grouping effects (low-score teammates) from communication score. - *This issue affects legitimate players who play silently or with minimal communication and still get punished unfairly. ### 🎯 Additional Context: Support Players Are Disproportionately Affected As a support player, I’ve noticed that the matchmaking system frequently pairs me with teammates (cores) that have very low performance or low behavior scores, despite my own account being at the maximum 12,000 behavior rating. This issue seems systemic: - Supports often have **no direct control over farming or game outcome**, yet are heavily affected by the quality of cores assigned to them. - The matchmaking algorithm appears to **prioritize balancing MMR globally** without considering role impact, resulting in **unfairly skewed lobbies** for high-behavior supports. - In practice, this leads to **consistent pairing with underperforming cores**, and therefore, **no MMR progress despite strong individual play and conduct**. This might explain why **high-behavior support players** experience: - Stagnation or decline in rank. - Frustration despite playing clean, communicative matches. - A perception that the system "punishes" supports who queue solo. I believe this deserves review, since role-based matchmaking should protect support players who maintain good behavior and consistent team contribution. ---
